summary: In commercial spaceflight, Virgin Galactic announced it has delayed the resumption of its commercial flights to 2027, while rocket builder Firefly reported record second-quarter financial results despite launch lags, and China’s iSpace raised new series E funding to advance its reusable rocketry. In military space developments, defense officials warned that the Pentagon's Golden Dome program faces a potential funding cliff in 2027, even as contractors cleared the initiative's first milestone and the U.S. Space Force ordered two additional Impulse Space vehicles for orbital maneuvering demonstrations. In civil space, NASA data is currently being utilized by commercial partners planning sustainable lunar habitation, while analysis of radiation-shielding vests tested during the Artemis I mission suggests the technology can effectively safeguard astronauts during solar storms. Furthermore, four-time spaceflight veteran Mike Fincke has officially departed NASA, and astronomers relying on James Webb Space Telescope data reported the discovery of the earliest known "black hole star." Internationally, millions of observers across the Arctic and Europe experienced a total solar eclipse, coinciding with SpaceX completing a mission to orbit 24 Starlink satellites from California. Looking ahead, skywatchers can expect favorable viewing conditions tonight as the annual Perseid meteor shower reaches its peak.
